views.visible: High aerial over a dry, rolling plain pitted with many round collapse sinkholes. Pale buff and olive ground, grey-green scrub gathered in the hollows and along the rims, thin haze to the horizon; a banded gas giant and two moons fill the sky.
views.subject: landscape
views.settingCue: Open dry plain with repeated sinkholes, not a canyon: broad low relief, scrub in swales and on rims, no built edge visible at this range.

views.visible: Downward view into a huge brown sinkhole. Ring after ring of pale built ledges, causeways and small structures follow the wall; the floor is dark and hazy, the rock face rough and vertically furrowed.
views.subject: settlement-edge
views.settingCue: Built settlement wrapping a sinkhole wall in stacked rings; dark rock face, pale platform edges, no flat ground visible.

views.visible: A sinkhole wall seen side-on: horizontal rock benches stacked in tiers, carrying round and ribbed pale city structures, a continuous walkway and a few smoking vents. One large ribbed sphere sits right of the walkway. No ground plane and no figures visible.
views.subject: settlement-edge
views.settingCue: Tiered rock benches used as building shelves inside a sinkhole; architecture sits on the strata, it does not cover the natural wall.

views.visible: Earth analogue (Xiaozhai Tiankeng, Chongqing, China, not Utapau): Near-vertical pale limestone cliff rims a very large collapse sinkhole. Dense green forest covers the floor far below; scrub and small trees hold ledges and cracks on the rim. Grey sky above.
views.subject: landscape
views.settingCue: Collapse sinkhole with sheer carbonate walls and a vegetated floor, used to read cliff shelves and the rim-to-floor transition.

views.visible: Earth analogue (Xiaozhai Difeng, Chongqing, China, not Utapau): A deep narrow gorge between grey limestone walls. Horizontal strata form continuous benches and undercuts; the floor is dark continuous forest. No water sheet visible.
views.subject: landscape
views.settingCue: Stratified limestone gorge with bench-like shelves and a forested floor, for wall layering rather than settlement.

views.visible: Earth analogue (Tsingy de Bemaraha, Madagascar, not Utapau): A dense field of sharp grey limestone blades and pinnacles separated by deep narrow fissures. Almost no soil; a little scrub in the shaded cracks, green plain beyond.
views.subject: landscape
views.settingCue: Eroded karst stone forest: bare, broken, near-vertical stone with almost no ground cover.

views.visible: Earth analogue (The Burren, Co. Clare, Ireland, not Utapau): Grey limestone slabs split into irregular blocks by deep grikes. Grass, moss and low herbs grow only in the cracks; scattered small stones on the bare rock. Flat horizon under a clear sky.
views.subject: landscape
views.settingCue: Bare flat pavement with fractured slabs and growth confined to joints, for stony ground at squad height.

views.visible: Earth analogue (Bisti/De-Na-Zin Wilderness, New Mexico, USA, not Utapau): Eroded pale and charcoal soft-rock hoodoos, capped spires and fins rise from a cracked, dark badland floor; sparse dry grass and a flat plain at the horizon.
views.subject: landscape
views.settingCue: Soft-rock spires and fins with undercut bases and a dry cracked floor, for the tall eroded forms seen on the mounted map.

views.visible: Earth analogue (Kasha-Katuwe Tent Rocks, New Mexico, USA, not Utapau): A cream and grey banded tuff shelf cut by a deep smooth gully. Two isolated trees stand on the pale floor; the exposed wall shows clear horizontal bedding and soft rounded erosion.
views.subject: landscape
views.settingCue: Banded soft-rock shelf and gully with isolated trees, for pale layered strata and a natural open pocket.

views.visible: Earth analogue (Matera, Basilicata, Italy, not Utapau): Cave dwellings cut directly into a pale rock slope, with masonry fronts, doors, small windows, steps and carved terraces stacked up the hillside. Weeds and small shrubs grow from ledges; a cobbled lane in front; modern pipework and two small signs.
views.subject: building
views.settingCue: Dwellings recessed into a rock face with built fronts on natural ledges, for architecture that follows the strata.

views.visible: Earth analogue (Garrigue, southern France, not Utapau): Low, dense woody scrub with small leathery leaves, dry grass and yellow flowers on a pale rocky limestone slope; taller dark shrubs behind.
views.subject: landscape
views.settingCue: Low woody scrub on stony ground with open gaps, for dry-land growth form and its scale.

ground.decision: Connect dry ochre grit around the rim. Local fines gather on lee ground; coarse lag sits in runnels, and inclined rock descends into the existing hole.
ground.reject: Reject lava, shiny wet beds, tiled red mud and an artificial floor across the dark sink.

foliage.decision: Retain the low bushes and isolated grass clumps where they already grow on the warm outer shelf. The silhouette of the sink stays open.
foliage.reject: No imported forest or uniform green pasture, even where wet terrestrial sinkholes support trees.

review.basis: The stock battle submits broad low leaf bushes and several arid shrub models plus one separate grass form. These are local pockets of vegetation, not a continuous planted landscape.

forms.form: Irregular, low woody clumps scattered across the open rim.
forms.silhouette: Small rounded tufts and spreading shrubs break the stone below the skyline.
forms.variation: Keep the differing leaf-bush and twiggy desert shapes at the real roots and scales.
forms.reason: The mounted shrubs already frame the clear approaches without hiding the lips.

forms.form: Low thin blades in discrete patches between stone and soil.
forms.silhouette: Short tufts stand below the spreading shrubs and buildings.
forms.variation: Retain the actual sparse grass placements; bare stone and deck surfaces interrupt them.
forms.reason: The grass prop is present on the dry map, not evidence of a swamp or water sheet.

place.where: Within the authored shrub and herb roots on the outside shelf, away from the large drop.

exclude.where: Over the central void, service deck and exposed inward wall.
exclude.reason: The decks and deep rock face are distinct from the growing substrate.

variation.decision: Preserve distinct small groups, scale changes and unplanted intervals rather than adding plants at grid spacing.
limits: Keep the sky and the platform edges open; no decorative crowns beyond the map.

landmark.decision: Preserve the open sink, its ribbed interior model and six walled platform tongues. Match worn concrete only to their painted extent.
landmark.reject: Do not reconstruct all of Pau City or add new inhabited decks around the circumference.

natural.decision: Loose dry mineral cover around both deployment areas; separate gravel and inclined fractured rock from open ground.

built.decision: Six contiguous concrete-painted footprints carry parapets or the fuel installation. Keep the two stock projections within those footprints; slot 62 also accepts real construction events.

transition.decision: An abrupt engineered lip at the projecting decks contrasts with the loose, unbuilt perimeter and the exposed internal cliff.

outskirts.skyline: Low rolling and sparsely broken ground beyond the real outer rim; the sink remains the only large opening on the battlefield.
outskirts.join: Meet all 1240 authored rim vertices with the shelf surface. No interior filler, new settlement or exported shrubs.
outskirts.reject: No second decorative sinkhole or wall of pinnacles; do not turn the map inside out.

climate.substrate: Ochre mineral sand and worn grit on the open ground of opposing launch shelves.
climate.lighting: Sunrise_Clear uses UTAPAU_SKYDOME and has no weather scenario. Keep the warm original daylight and its shadows.
climate.exceptions: The covered deck, local coarse runnels, shaded sidewalls and authored interior are different surfaces, not discolored bare ground.

pairs.basis: Clear shelf behind the southeast formation, between the parapet and rock clusters.
Two open sandy patches above the opposite muster, inset from the dark shrubs and deck edge.

uncertain: The photographs constrain shape and placement, not an exact mineral species or an engineering plan for the fictional city. The stock map models only a small set of platforms.
